issues.symptom: Original room has open floor plan with distinct zones; render shows generic bedroom. Ceiling fixture, window treatment, and wall proportions differ significantly. Floor appears same but room function completely changed.

COVABIOPHILIC style emphasizes organic materials, biophilic elements, and natural integration. Render shows minimal plant life (single potted plant), minimal natural materials, lacks the warm organic aesthetic requested.
Bed appears flat and dimensionally awkward. Bedding materials lack texture depth. Nightstand proportions seem off relative to bed scale. Chair geometry looks simplified.
Sparse composition with heavy reliance on bed as focal point. Mid-ground and background underpopulated. Lacks layering and visual interest compared to benchmark's balanced multi-zone approach.
Ceiling light is bright but casts minimal shadows. Window light quality inconsistent. Lacks warm accent lighting and layered lighting hierarchy seen in benchmark.
Bedding lacks weave texture. Wall art is indistinct. Plant leaf definition poor. Nightstand surface lacks material specificity. Some geometry softening suggests AI smoothing artifacts.
Render lacks design intentionality and visual narrative. Appears as generic contemporary bedroom rather than curated space. Color palette uninspired compared to benchmark's cohesive aesthetic.
Ignores original room's open-concept, dual-purpose layout. Eliminates DAKSH branding context. Doesn't acknowledge original furniture pieces or spatial configuration.
Benchmark demonstrates superior spatial planning, material authenticity, layered styling, and editorial sophistication. Render underperforms across aesthetic and functional dimensions.
